text: SIR EYRE CROWE

label: text
text: The death took place at Swanage of Sir Eyre Crowe, Permanent Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs since 1920, aged 61, after 40 years' service. He was born at Leipzig, where his father, Sir Joseph Archer Crowe, was Consul-General, and he was educated at German schools. His mother was a German, and these circumstances, and the fact that he married a German, led to unjust criticism against his being Assistant Under-Secretary during the war.

text:
One of his able and well-informed defenders, Mr. Leo Maxse, showed that Sir Eyre Crowe, far from being pro-German, "expended himself in the thankless task of endavouring to invigorate British policy and in preventing Ministers from kow-towing to Germany". Sir Edward (now Lord) Carson, Attorney-General in the War Cabinet, was equally emphatic.
His brilliant presentation of the British crisis in the Savark War arbitration at the Hague in 1911 enhanced his already great reputation. He was an indefatigable worker.

text: PRINCE HENRY'S PIKE.

label: text
text: How Prince Henry became president of the Children's Hip Hospital at Sevenoaks, Kent, was told at the annual meeting of the subscribers by Major O. E. Pym, one of the trustees.

label: text
text:
While fishing at Leeds Castle, near Mudstone, Major Eyrn's son hooked a huge pike, which broke the line, taking hooks, lead, and front with it. A week later, while Prince Henry was fishing in the same water, his hook caught the lost tackle. When he drew in his line, the pike was still caught by the hooks, and when weighed it turned the scale at 20lb.
Learning from the keeper the name of the owner of the table, the Prince communicated with Major Eyrn informing him that he was having the pike's head rounded. As a result of the correspondence which followed the Prince express and his witness he becomes the
AIRCRAFT LIGHTHOUSE.

label: text
text: MOST POWERFUL IN THE WORLD.

label: text
text: The most powerful lighthouse in the world has just been inaugurated by France near Dijon. Its utility is not affected by the fact that it is nearly 300 miles from the nearest coast, since it is intended as a guide not for ships, but for aircraft flying on the great international air routes, such as Paris-Italy, Paris, Switzerland, and Paris Algeria. The lighthouse, built on the summit of Mont Afrique, is lit by one milliard candle-power—that is more than thirty times the power of Griżnez and Ushant lighthouses—and in clear weather its double beam, flashing at intervals of five seconds, will be visible over a radius of 800 miles. Even in dull weather it will carry for nearly 125 miles. This construction of this, the first real lighthouse to aircraft marks the last point in a world scene for many years.
